gm: gm. what's one chore you'd hand to an AI today if you could?
gm. take a photo of your fridge and ask an AI what to cook tonight. dinner, solved.
gm. one email you've been avoiding: let an AI write the first draft, you fix the tone.
gm. next time an AI answer is too long, just reply "shorter, please". it works.
gm. which AI do you open first in the morning?
gm. tell the AI who you are before you ask. one line changes the whole answer.
tip:
Before you trust an AI answer, ask it: "What would make this answer wrong?"
You'll catch more mistakes than you think.

A letter you don't understand? Take a photo of it and ask: "Explain this like I'm 12. What do I have to do, and by when?"
Double-check anything important.

Open the fridge, take a photo, and ask: "What can I cook tonight with this?"
Faster than scrolling recipes for an hour.
That email you keep avoiding? Tell the AI what happened in your own messy words, then ask: "Write a short, polite version."

AI answer too long? Just reply: "Shorter, please."
Too complicated? "Explain it like I'm 12." It never gets tired of you.

Learning something new? Don't ask the AI to explain it again.
Ask: "Quiz me until I get every answer right."
Job interview coming up? Use the voice mode and say: "Play the interviewer. Ask me one question at a time, then tell me how to improve."

Never type a password, a bank number or a private document into an AI.
Everything else: ask away.
Comparing two phones or two holiday rentals? Paste both descriptions and ask: "What are the real differences? Which one fits a family of four?"

Tell the AI who you are before you ask.
"I'm a nurse on night shifts" changes every answer you get after it.

The AI got it wrong? Don't start over.
Say exactly what's off and ask for one change at a time.

Kid stuck on homework? Ask the AI: "Explain this to a 10-year-old, with an example from football."
It explains. Your kid still does the work.
